crime: Every dusk, a girl sang for the courtyard from the upper railing. She had run out of songs from home within a week. After that, {WITCH_NAME} gave her new ones: her own songs, whispered line by line from across the mansion, straight into the girl's ear. No one else knew.
At the railing one evening before dusk, the girl told her with a smile, "Tomorrow I'll sing one of my own. You can rest."
{WITCH_NAME}'s mother had once hummed the harmony under every song her daughter sang. Then she said, "You can carry it alone now," and was gone within the week.

That dusk, {WITCH_NAME} whispered one last song into the girl's ear: "Don't wait up. I'm going down to the water." The girl sang it to the courtyard line by line, filmed from below as she was every dusk.
After dusk, {WITCH_NAME} whispered to her again, calling her down to the lake shore for a proper goodbye. There she held the girl's face under the water until she went still.
In the trial court, the prisoners took the song as the girl's own goodbye: she had walked into the lake.
Then a prisoner replayed the last song on her phone. Before every line, the singer turned her ear toward her empty shoulder.
The prisoners understood. The goodbye had been {WITCH_NAME}'s, and so had the water.
fields.epitaph: Of all those songs, she was asked only to listen to one, and never heard it: the girl's own.
execution: The execution stand raises an iron stage in the trial court. She is chained kneeling in the prompter's slot at its edge, her head and shoulders just under the line of the iron curtain.
An iron singer sings the song straight through, never waiting for her lines. She mouths each one a beat behind.
The iron curtain comes down onto her shoulders. It does not stop. It keeps coming down, pressing her into the slot.
It comes to rest, shut against the stage floor. Nothing stirs beneath it.

magic.name: Right Beside You
magic.text: She can speak or sing into anyone's ear from any distance, and only they hear her.
